subject: Hosted API degraded: increased latency and error rates (Mar 9)
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lane <sophie@finova.com>
Cc: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 Mar 2025 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API degraded: increased latency and error rates (Mar 9)

Hi Sophie,

We're reaching out to let Finova know we're currently investigating increased latency and a spike in 5xx error rates affecting the Redwood hosted generation API in us-west-2. We opened an incident on our status page and wanted to make sure your team is aware: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2025-03-09-hosted-latency

What we know so far:
- Degraded throughput began at ~07:48 PDT (03:48 UTC)
- Error rate for text-generation routes peaked at ~12%
- No evidence of data exfiltration; logs show normal request routing and no unauthorized access

Immediate actions we have in progress:
- Engineering is rolling back a recent runtime optimization on a subset of hosts
- Affected hosts are being drained and traffic is being shifted to healthy capacity
- We're running targeted retries and throttling to limit impact to end-users

We will provide updates every 30 minutes or sooner if there's a material change. If you'd like a quick sync call, tell me a preferred window and I will set it up.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this affects your users. We will follow up with a post-incident summary and proposed service credit for the window of impact.

Thanks,
Lauren
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie — Lauren, quick engineering update below.

On Sun, Mar 9, 2025 at 8:15 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai> wrote:
> We're reaching out to let Finova know we're currently investigating increased latency...

Root cause (preliminary): a runtime optimization (asynchronous KV cache eviction) pushed earlier today caused contention in the token-cache hot-path under a specific request pattern. Under higher-concurrency traffic the eviction path introduced CPU stalls which cascaded to queue build-up and 5xx responses.

Mitigations underway:
- Rolling back the optimization (started 08:20 PDT) to restore the prior stable code path
- Draining and reprovisioning ~24 instances that showed persistent CPU saturation
- Temporarily increasing autoscale headroom in us-west-2 for generation endpoints

We do not see any logs indicating that request bodies or customer data were copied off-host. All access logs remain within expected identity principals.

ETA: partial recovery expected within 20–40 minutes after rollback completes; full stabilization may take up to 2 hours while caches warm up. I will post another update when we hit 50% and 90% recovery thresholds.

Grace
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lane <sophie@finova.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 Mar 2025 09:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API degraded: increased latency and error rates (Mar 9)

Update: rollback completed at 08:48 PDT and we observed a rapid decline in 5xx rates.

Metrics snapshot at 09:02 PDT:
- Error rate down from 12% to 1.3% on generation routes
- P99 latency reduced from ~2.4s to ~650ms
- Traffic fully routed off the 24 saturated instances by 08:55 PDT

We're continuing to monitor; there may be intermittent traces while caches repopulate. No customer data exposure detected.

If you'd like to join a quick 15-min call to walk the timeline and mitigations, I'll be available at 09:30 PDT.

— Dylan
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lane <sophie@finova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Mar 2025 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — Hosted API (Mar 9)

Hi Sophie — following up with the post-incident summary and next steps. Apologies again for the disruption on Sunday. Please find the high-level notes below and the full postmortem attached.

Summary:
- Impact window: 2025-03-09 07:48 — 2025-03-09 09:05 PDT
- Effect: elevated latency and increased 5xx errors for hosted generation endpoints in us-west-2
- Root cause: contention introduced by a runtime KV cache eviction optimization under certain concurrency patterns
- Customer data: no evidence of exfiltration or improper access

What we did:
- Rolled back the change and drained saturated hosts
- Increased autoscale headroom temporarily
- Added additional automated circuit-breakers to prevent the optimization from activating under high-concurrency patterns

Customer impact & remediation:
- We are offering a service credit equivalent to 1 day of hosted-generation credits for Finova; attached is a preliminary SLA credit quote (sla-credit-quote-20250310.pdf).
- Full postmortem (redwood-postmortem-20250309.pdf) is attached and a read-only copy is available here: https://drive.google.com/finova-postmortem-20250309

Action items (owners):
- Engineering: add a canary gating step for runtime optimizations (Dylan)
- Platform: automated alert refinement for cache-path saturation (Grace)
- Account: coordinate credit and formal notification (Lauren / Marissa)

If you'd like an executive summary for your leadership, we can prepare a 1-page note. We can also schedule a walkthrough with Engineering next week to go through technical details.

Again, I'm sorry for the outage and appreciate your patience.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-postmortem-20250309.pdf, sla-credit-quote-20250310.pdf
